text: {"lessons":["Repeatedly selling Stock A and Stock C after gains may reflect a desire to lock in profits; I should judge each holding by its current risk and role, not by whether it feels like a win.","After the account fell in Periods 9 and 10, doing nothing may have been reasonable, but I should still review whether my allocation fits my plan instead of letting discomfort or attachment to my purchase price decide.","Frequent checking and trading can encourage impulsive decisions even when prices are unpredictable; I should use clear portfolio rules and trade only when they call for it."]}
